issues.legal_issue: A conviction cannot be sustained when eyewitness evidence is inadequate without corroboration and the alleged dying declaration is not reliably established.
material_facts: The convictions for murder with common intention and rioting were upheld on appeal, with the alleged dying declaration serving as corroboration for eyewitness accounts.

One eyewitness did not support the prosecution, and the other eyewitness accounts were treated as inadequate without corroboration; several witnesses had connections to the parties or the underlying disputes.
The deceased’s son and nephew testified that the deceased briefly regained consciousness and identified the attackers, including by describing piercing injuries.
The post-mortem evidence described the head wounds as lacerated wounds caused by a blunt weapon and did not support the account of piercing injuries.
The doctor testified that brain congestion from the head injuries meant the deceased might not have regained consciousness after losing it.
issues.conclusion: The alleged dying declaration was not proved with sufficient reliability to corroborate the eyewitness accounts. Since those accounts were inadequate without corroboration, the accused were entitled to the benefit of the doubt; the appeal was allowed and the convictions were set aside, with acquittals on both charges.
issues.legal_principle: A dying declaration cannot serve as corroboration unless the evidence reliably establishes that it was made. Where medical evidence undermines the account of the declaration or casts serious doubt on whether the deceased could have made it, and the eyewitness evidence is inadequate on its own, the accused are entitled to the benefit of the doubt. The Court applied this reasoning to convictions under Sections 302 read with 34 and 148 of the Indian Penal Code. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_appeal and eyewitness_evidence_lacked_independent_support and declaration_was_reported_by_relatives and (medical_evidence_conflicted_with_declaration or medical_evidence_cast_doubt_on_consciousness)

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding was a criminal appeal challenging convictions.
predicates.eyewitness_evidence_lacked_independent_s: The eyewitness accounts included a witness who did not support the prosecution and accounts the appellate court regarded as inadequate without corroboration.
predicates.declaration_was_reported_by_relatives: The alleged declaration was recounted by the deceased’s son and nephew, who said the deceased regained consciousness and identified the attackers.
predicates.medical_evidence_conflicted_with_declara: The medical examination described wounds inconsistent with the reported account of piercing injuries.
predicates.medical_evidence_cast_doubt_on_conscious: The doctor testified that the deceased might not have regained consciousness after losing it.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction appeal involves eyewitness evidence lacking independent support and a declaration reported by relatives that is undermined by medical evidence or by medical doubt about the deceased’s consciousness, the accused are entitled to acquittal.
